shorts.hook: Cassowaries have killed people. Most attacks start with a snack.
shorts.title: Most Cassowary Attacks Come From Birds People Fed First
shorts.outro: Four bigger animals were still waiting. The full video is linked below.
shorts.description: In a study of 150 cassowary attacks on people in Queensland, three in four came from birds that had been fed before, so Doug brings birdseed and runs out.

shorts.hook: Doug tried to out-chest-beat a silverback gorilla.
shorts.title: A Gorilla's Chest Beat Tells Rivals Exactly How Big It Is
shorts.outro: The next animal did not walk away. The full video is linked below.
shorts.description: Bigger silverbacks drum their chests at a lower pitch that carries over a kilometer, so when Doug beats his own chest back, the gorilla does the arithmetic.

shorts.hook: Elephants can tell a dangerous human from his voice alone.
shorts.title: Elephants Know If You're a Threat Just From Your Voice
shorts.outro: That was Doug's one hundredth death. All ten fights are in the full video.
shorts.description: Elephants in Kenya's Amboseli National Park can judge from a human voice alone whether the speaker is dangerous, and Doug's one hundredth death proves it doesn't always help.
